hook: Thieves stole a heritage plaque at Portchester Castle, erasing a vital piece of British history.

sections.voiceover: Thieves stole a heritage plaque at Portchester Castle, erasing a vital piece of British history.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up shot of an empty stone wall at Portchester Castle where a plaque was recently mounted.
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle wind ambient with a sharp mechanical click.
b_roll: Portchester Castle exterior stone walls in Hampshire

sections.voiceover: On Friday 9 October 2026, Portchester Castle in Hampshire unveiled a memorial plaque. That bronze marker honored 2,500 African-Caribbean prisoners brought to Britain in 1796. Castle staff made a grim discovery on Wednesday 14 October 2026. Where did the memorial plaque go?
sections.visual_cue: Archival photograph of Portchester Castle grounds transitioning to the unveiling banner.
b_roll: University of Warwick press release document
BBC News article snippet showing Portchester Castle

sections.voiceover: Worse, thieves stole the memorial plaque and a gate padlock just five days later.
sections.visual_cue: Macro shot of a rusted iron padlock hanging from a heavy wooden castle gate.
b_roll: Close up of castle gate fittings

sections.voiceover: Five days after the ceremony, the bronze marker vanished completely.
sections.visual_cue: Newspaper clipping from The Guardian detailing the stolen memorial.
sections.sfx_cue: Paper rustling and police siren fade-in.

sections.voiceover: Those 2,500 prisoners remain etched into British history.
sections.visual_cue: Wide establishing shot of Portchester Castle against the Hampshire sky.
